description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:Build the capacity of religious and traditional leaders, as well as women and youth, to promote tolerance and prevent violent conflict and extremism in their communities;Foster the rights of religious and ethnic minorities by initiating various interventions to address interethnic and interreligious conflict; andWork with local stakeholders to create and support community-based early warning, early response (EWER) systems.The Community Initiatives to Promote Peace (CIPP) activity implements quick impact initiatives aimed at bringing communities together to promote peace and stability in Benue, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kogi, and Plateau states. This activity will work with Nigerian government institutions (such as the Human Rights Commission) and private sector actors at all levels to build the sustainability of early response systems and strengthen the capacity of relevant organizations to identify and address religious issues. Maintaining gender-sensitive methodologies and gender integration, the activity also elevates women's unique role in preventing and mitigating conflict by integrating women leaders into local community- and state-level peace structures. These actions will strengthen the capacity of communities to promote communal resilience against conflict and religious freedom in target states. These results align with key priorities of the Integrated Country Strategy for Nigeria and are key U.S. foreign policy priorities for the region, specifically Goals 1-3 of the 2022-2026 Joint Strategic Plan..
